sections.title: Part 1 · Listening to Problem Solving
sections.instructions: Listen to the conversation and answer the questions.
sections.passage:
AGENT: Thank you for calling Northern Sky Travel, this is Priya speaking.
CUSTOMER: Hi Priya, my name is Jordan Ellis. My flight to Halifax tomorrow morning was cancelled, and all I got was an automated text with no details.
AGENT: Let me pull up your booking. Yes, I see it. The airline cancelled every departure from Toronto before ten a.m. because of the storm that's forecast overnight.
CUSTOMER: That's a problem. I'm presenting at a conference in Halifax at one o'clock tomorrow afternoon.
AGENT: I understand. I have three options. First, the same flight on Friday at eight-fifteen a.m. Second, a reroute this evening, leaving at six-forty through Montreal and landing in Halifax at eleven fifty-five tonight. Or third, a full refund.
CUSTOMER: Friday is too late, so that rules out the first one. Is there any extra charge for the reroute?
AGENT: Normally there's a sixty-dollar change fee, but the airline is waiving it because of the weather.
CUSTOMER: Good. What about my seat?
AGENT: On the Montreal flight, I can give you a window seat. On the second leg, only middle seats are left.
CUSTOMER: I can live with a middle seat for the second leg. Let's book it.
AGENT: Done. I recommend arriving at the airport by four-forty, two hours before departure. I can't contact your hotel, so you'll want to let them know you'll be checking in around midnight.
CUSTOMER: I'll call them right now. Thanks, Priya.

questions.label: Question 1
questions.question: Why is Jordan calling?
options: A booking was made under the wrong name
The hotel in Halifax cancelled a reservation
Jordan wants to upgrade to a window seat
A flight was cancelled and the text message gave no details
questions.explanation: Jordan received only an automated text with no details about the cancellation.

questions.label: Question 2
questions.question: Why did the airline cancel the flights?
options: The airport is closing for repairs

questions.explanation: The agent says the cancellation is because of the storm forecast overnight.

questions.explanation: Jordan presents tomorrow at one o'clock, so a Friday flight is too late.

questions.explanation: Jordan says "Let's book it" after asking about the reroute.

questions.label: Question 5

options: Jordan must pay sixty dollars at the airport

options: An aisle seat on the first flight only

questions.explanation: The Montreal leg has a window seat; only middle seats remain on the second leg.

questions.explanation: The agent cannot contact the hotel, so Jordan must let them know about the late arrival.

sections.passage: ANNOUNCER: The regional transit authority announced today that fares will rise five percent starting July first, the first increase in three years. An adult monthly pass will go from one hundred twenty dollars to one hundred twenty-six dollars, while single-ride fares will stay at three dollars and twenty-five cents until next January. Children under thirteen will continue to ride free. Authority chair Denise Alvarez said the added revenue will help pay for forty new buses and extend evening service on eleven routes. HANNAH: Thanks for coming, everyone. We've received a two-thousand-dollar grant, and we have to decide how to spend it before the end of the month.
OMAR: I'd like to put it toward playground equipment. The swings at Oak Street Park have been broken since the fall, and there are lots of young families on our block.
BETH: I understand, but I think street lighting is more urgent. Three residents told me they no longer walk through the laneway after dark.
HANNAH: Lighting is a safety issue. Solar lights for the laneway would cost about twelve hundred dollars.
OMAR: And new swings would be around eighteen hundred, so we can't do both.
BETH: What if the city repairs the swings? Playground maintenance is technically their responsibility. Someone could call the parks department.
OMAR: I did call, twice. They said the repair is on a list for next year.
HANNAH: Then here's a thought. We use the grant for the lighting now, and Omar leads a petition asking the city to fix the swings sooner. We'd have eight hundred dollars left, which we could set aside toward the playground.
OMAR: That's reasonable, as long as the leftover money is set aside specifically for the playground.
BETH: Agreed. I can get quotes from two lighting companies by next Wednesday.
HANNAH: Great. Let's hold the vote at the meeting on the twenty-first.

SPEAKER A: I'm convinced a four-day work week is the future. A company in my city switched last year, kept everyone's pay the same, and found that output didn't drop at all. Employees were less stressed, and resignations fell by almost a third.
SPEAKER B: I don't think it works everywhere. Hospitals, restaurants, and customer service centres can't just shut down for an extra day. Either they hire more staff, which costs money, or workers cram forty hours into four long days, which is exhausting.
SPEAKER A: That's true for some sectors, but it isn't an argument against the idea overall. Offices and tech firms could adopt it tomorrow, and that would put pressure on other industries to find creative scheduling.
SPEAKER B: Maybe, but I worry about fairness. If office workers get a three-day weekend while nurses and cashiers don't, we widen the gap between people who have flexibility and people who don't.
SPEAKER A: I see the concern, but I'd say the answer is to extend the benefit gradually, not to deny it to everyone.

From: Samira Khan <s.khan@northgate-eng.com>
To: Human Resources <hr@northgate-eng.com>
Subject: Relocation to the Calgary office

Dear HR team,

I am writing to confirm the details of my transfer to the Calgary office. My manager, Tyrone Blake, told me the move was approved on February 12, and I would like to start on May 6 if possible. I have a few questions about the relocation package.

First, is the $3,000 relocation allowance paid in advance, or reimbursed after I submit receipts? Second, my lease in Toronto ends on May 31, so I may need temporary housing in Calgary for a few weeks. Finally, my partner will be moving with me. Does the package cover her flight as well?

Thank you,
Samira Khan

------------------------------

From: Olivia Grant <hr@northgate-eng.com>
To: Samira Khan
Subject: Re: Relocation to the Calgary office

Dear Samira,

Congratulations on the transfer! May 6 is fine with us. To answer your questions:

The $3,000 allowance is reimbursed, not paid upfront, so please keep all receipts and submit them within 30 days of your start date. Temporary housing is covered for up to 30 days in a company-approved corporate apartment; you would need to book at least two weeks in advance through our travel coordinator. Your partner's airfare is also covered, but only one-way, and only if it is booked on the same day as your own ticket. Movers are not included in the package, although you may claim up to $500 for boxes and packing supplies under the allowance.

Please return the signed relocation agreement by April 12. You will also receive five paid days off for the move. Note that if your Toronto lease runs past your start date, you will be responsible for the overlapping rent.

Best regards,
Olivia Grant
Human Resources

sections.title: Reading Part 3 · Reading for Information
sections.instructions: Read the article and answer the questions.
sections.passageTitle: Cool cities: the case for urban trees
sections.passage:
Cities are often several degrees hotter than the countryside around them. This "urban heat island" effect occurs because dark surfaces such as asphalt and rooftops absorb sunlight during the day and release it slowly at night, sometimes keeping urban neighbourhoods up to five degrees warmer after dark.

Trees offer one of the most affordable defences. Their leaves provide shade, and they cool the air by releasing moisture. Research suggests that neighbourhoods with about thirty percent tree canopy can be up to four degrees cooler than those with little cover. Trees also absorb stormwater, which reduces flooding, and they filter fine particles from the air.

Despite these benefits, many cities are losing trees. A recent survey of mid-sized cities found canopy cover shrinking by an average of one percent a year, as old trees die and new construction removes others.

Planting alone does not solve the problem. Nearly half of street trees die within ten years, largely because of compacted soil, road salt, and too little water. Urban foresters recommend planting a diverse mix of species so that one disease cannot wipe out a whole street, and giving each tree a larger volume of good soil in which to grow.

Some cities are turning to residents for help. In adopt-a-tree programs, neighbours agree to water young trees during dry spells. Cities that pair planting with this kind of follow-up care have seen survival rates climb to around 85 percent, suggesting that the cheapest way to grow a canopy is to look after the trees already planted.

questions.label: Question 1
questions.question: What is the main idea of the article?
options: Urban trees help cool cities but need proper care to survive
Cities should stop building with asphalt
Countryside areas are always cooler than cities
Tree planting is too expensive for most cities
questions.explanation: The article explains the benefits of trees and stresses that planting must be paired with care.

questions.label: Question 2
questions.question: Why are cities hotter than the countryside?
options: There is less wind in the countryside
Dark surfaces absorb sunlight and release heat slowly at night
Buildings block the sun and trap moisture
Cities have more people breathing out heat
questions.explanation: Asphalt and rooftops absorb sunlight and release it slowly.

questions.question: How much cooler can a neighbourhood with about thirty percent canopy be?
questions.explanation: The article says up to four degrees cooler.

questions.label: Question 4

options: They absorb stormwater and reduce flooding
They produce fuel for city buses
questions.explanation: Trees absorb stormwater, which reduces flooding.

questions.label: Question 5

options: It is growing by one percent a year
It is shrinking by about one percent a year
It is shrinking by ten percent a year
questions.explanation: The survey found an average one percent yearly decline.

questions.label: Question 6
questions.question: Why do many street trees die?
options: Compacted soil, road salt, and too little water
questions.explanation: The article lists compacted soil, road salt, and lack of water.

questions.label: Question 7

options: Using more road salt near trees
Planting diverse species and providing more soil
questions.explanation: They recommend mixed species and larger soil volumes.

questions.label: Question 8
questions.question: What have cities that add follow-up care seen?
options: Tree planting costs falling by half
Survival rates rising to about 85 percent
Canopy cover doubling in a year
questions.explanation: Cities pairing planting with care report survival around 85 percent.

questions.question: Which best describes the author's attitude?
options: Doubtful that trees make any difference
Supportive of tree planting but realistic about its challenges
questions.explanation: The author praises trees while pointing out that most planting fails without care.

sections.title: Reading Part 4 · Reading for Viewpoints
sections.instructions: Read the two viewpoints and answer the questions.
sections.passage:
Lock Them Away
By Elaine Ward

Smartphones have no place in the classroom. When our district introduced a school-day phone ban two years ago, average test scores rose by six percent and reported cyberbullying incidents dropped by a third. Teachers who once spent fifteen minutes a day policing screens now spend that time teaching. Just as important, students started talking to one another at lunch again. Parents worry about reaching their children in an emergency, but the school office has always been able to do that. A ban is not about punishment. It is about giving young people a break from constant notifications so they can focus and connect.

Teach, Don't Ban
By Marcus Bell

A blanket ban treats a useful tool as if it were only a threat. For students with learning disabilities, phones provide text-to-speech, translation, and note-taking support that few classroom substitutes can match. Many families also rely on phones to coordinate pickups and after-school care. Schools that adopted locked pouches found that students simply carried second, cheaper phones or waited for the moment the pouches were opened. Instead of banning devices, schools should teach digital literacy and set clear rules for each class, so students learn to manage the distractions they will face for the rest of their lives.

questions.question: What is the main topic of the two pieces?
options: Whether smartphones should be banned in schools
questions.explanation: Both authors discuss banning phones during the school day.

questions.label: Question 2
questions.question: What happened to test scores after the ban, according to Ward?
questions.explanation: Ward reports average scores rose by six percent.

questions.label: Question 3
questions.question: What happened to reported cyberbullying?
questions.explanation: Ward says incidents dropped by a third.

questions.label: Question 4

options: They train students in digital skills
questions.explanation: Ward says teachers spend that time teaching.

options: Students may keep phones in their bags

questions.explanation: She says the school office has always been able to contact children.

questions.label: Question 6
questions.question: How does Ward describe the purpose of a ban?
options: Giving students a break from notifications so they can focus and connect
questions.explanation: She says a ban is about focus and connection, not punishment.

questions.label: Question 7
questions.question: Which students does Bell say benefit especially from phones?
questions.explanation: Bell mentions text-to-speech, translation, and note-taking support for students with learning disabilities.

questions.label: Question 8
questions.question: What did schools that used locked pouches discover?
questions.explanation: Students carried second phones or waited until pouches opened.

questions.label: Question 9
questions.question: What does Bell recommend instead of a ban?
options: Teaching digital literacy and setting clear rules per class
Giving every student a school tablet
questions.explanation: He recommends digital literacy and class-by-class rules.

questions.label: Question 10
questions.question: Which statement would both authors most likely agree with?
options: Phones can distract students from learning
Phones should be banned in every classroom
questions.explanation: Ward says students need a break from notifications and Bell speaks of managing distractions; both see phones as potentially distracting.

Ask for a solution, such as another section or a refund.
Keep a polite and professional tone.
writingTask.sampleAnswer: Dear Ms. Alvarez, I am writing about the Adult Pottery class I registered for, which was scheduled for Tuesday evenings at 7:00 p.m. Yesterday I received a notice that the class has been moved to Tuesday afternoons at 2:00 p.m., starting next week. Unfortunately, I work until 5:00 p.m. every weekday, so I will no longer be able to attend. I paid the $95 fee three weeks ago, and I was looking forward to the course, so this change is very disappointing. I would like to ask whether there is another section available in the evening, or whether the class could remain at its original time. If neither option is possible, I would appreciate a full refund of my registration fee. Please let me know what you can offer as soon as possible, since the first session is only six days away. I can be reached by email or at 555-0142. Thank you for your time and understanding. Sincerely, Jamie Rowe

sections.title: Writing Task 2 · Survey Response
sections.instructions: Write a response to the survey questions below.

writingTask.title: Responding to Survey Questions
writingTask.scenario: Your employer has a $50,000 budget for staff and is asking employees to choose between building a wellness room with exercise equipment and quiet space, or funding professional development courses. Complete the survey explaining which option you prefer and why.
instructions: Give at least two reasons for your choice.
Suggest one improvement to your preferred option.
writingTask.sampleAnswer: I would choose the professional development fund. Although a wellness room would be pleasant, courses give staff skills that benefit both employees and the company. First, training helps people advance. Many of my colleagues want to move into leadership roles but lack the certifications to apply, and funding would remove that barrier. Second, better-trained employees make fewer mistakes and work more efficiently, so the investment pays for itself over time. A wellness room, by contrast, would be used by only part of the staff and would bring ongoing maintenance costs. To improve the plan, I suggest letting each employee apply for up to $1,500 and asking them to share what they learned in a short lunchtime presentation. That way the whole team benefits from every course. I also recommend surveying staff first to see which topics are most in demand. Thank you for asking for our input.

sections.title: Speaking Task 1 · Giving Advice
sections.instructions: Prepare and speak using the prompt below.

speakingTask.title: Task 1: Giving Advice
speakingTask.scenario: Your friend has a job interview next week for a position they really want, and they are very nervous. Give your friend advice on how to prepare and how to make a good impression.
tips: Give two or three specific, practical suggestions.
Use a warm, encouraging tone.
Explain briefly why each suggestion helps.
speakingTask.sampleAnswer: If I were you, I would start by researching the company thoroughly, because knowing its projects and values lets you give answers that fit. Next, practise out loud with a friend, using common questions like "Tell me about yourself." That way you will sound confident instead of rehearsed. On the day, arrive fifteen minutes early, dress neatly, and bring a few thoughtful questions of your own. Finally, remember that the interviewers want you to succeed, so take a deep breath and be yourself. I'm sure you'll do great.

sections.title: Speaking Task 2 · Talking about a Personal Experience
sections.instructions: Prepare and speak using the prompt below.

speakingTask.title: Task 2: Talking about a Personal Experience
speakingTask.scenario: Talk about a time when you had to work with a team to accomplish something difficult. Describe what happened and how it turned out.
tips: Set the scene quickly.
Explain your role and the challenge.
Finish with the result and what you learned.
speakingTask.sampleAnswer: Two years ago, my team at work had to finish a client report in just three days after a colleague fell ill. At first we were overwhelmed, so I suggested splitting the report by section and meeting briefly each morning. Everyone took ownership, and we caught several errors early. We delivered the report on time, and the client praised its clarity. I learned that clear communication and shared responsibility can turn a stressful situation into a real success.

sections.title: Speaking Task 3 · Describing a Scene
sections.instructions: Prepare and speak using the prompt below.

speakingTask.title: Task 3: Describing a Scene
speakingTask.scenario: Describe a train station at rush hour on a weekday morning. Include what you can see and hear and what people are doing.
tips: Move through the scene in a logical order.
Use vivid, specific vocabulary.
Mention at least two details of what people are doing.
speakingTask.sampleAnswer: The station is packed with commuters, and the air hums with the sound of footsteps and announcements. On the left, a long line of people waits to buy coffee, while others hurry toward the platforms with briefcases and backpacks. A train pulls in with a loud screech, and the doors open as passengers spill out. Near the clock, a man checks his phone anxiously and a student is running to catch the next departure. Despite the rush, there is a strangely organized rhythm to it all.

sections.title: Speaking Task 4 · Making Predictions
sections.instructions: Prepare and speak using the prompt below.

speakingTask.title: Task 4: Making Predictions
speakingTask.scenario: A family is loading suitcases into their car for a road trip while dark clouds gather overhead. The children are holding a picnic basket. Predict what will happen next and explain why.
tips: Use language of prediction such as will, probably, and likely.
Base each prediction on details in the scene.
Give a clear beginning, middle, and end.
speakingTask.sampleAnswer: I think the family will probably leave anyway, because the car is already packed and the children look excited. However, the dark clouds suggest heavy rain is coming soon, so the parents will likely turn on the wipers and drive slowly. Because of the weather, they will probably eat their picnic in the car or at a covered rest stop instead of outdoors. In the end, I believe the trip will still be fun, and the children will remember the rainy picnic as a funny story.

sections.title: Speaking Task 5 · Comparing and Persuading
sections.instructions: Prepare and speak using the prompt below.

speakingTask.title: Task 5: Comparing and Persuading
speakingTask.scenario: Your family is choosing between two vacations. Option A is a five-day beach resort with meals included, for $1,800. Option B is a five-day guided tour of a European city with museums and walking, for $2,200. Persuade your family to choose one option and explain why it is better.
tips: State your choice clearly at the start.
Compare the two options directly.
Use persuasive language and finish with a strong closing line.
speakingTask.sampleAnswer: I strongly recommend the beach resort. First, it is four hundred dollars cheaper, and that savings could pay for a nice family dinner or a boat trip. Second, with meals included, nobody has to plan or argue about where to eat. The city tour sounds interesting, but five days of walking and museums could be tiring, especially for the kids. After a stressful year, what we need most is rest and time together. So let's choose the resort and come home relaxed.

sections.title: Speaking Task 6 · Dealing with a Difficult Situation
sections.instructions: Prepare and speak using the prompt below.

speakingTask.title: Task 6: Dealing with a Difficult Situation
speakingTask.scenario: You organized a dinner for twelve guests to celebrate a colleague's retirement. When you arrive at the restaurant, the manager says your reservation was lost and no table is available. Explain what you would say to the manager and what you would do next.
tips: Stay calm and polite.
Explain the problem clearly and propose a solution.
Describe what you would do if the manager cannot help.
speakingTask.sampleAnswer: I would stay calm and tell the manager politely that I made the reservation two weeks ago and even have a confirmation email. I would explain that twelve guests are arriving for a retirement dinner, so this is very important. Then I would ask whether they could combine tables or offer a private room, even in thirty minutes. If that is not possible, I would ask them to recommend a nearby restaurant and call ahead for me. Finally, I would let my guests know about the delay so the evening still feels welcoming.

sections.title: Speaking Task 7 · Expressing Opinions
sections.instructions: Prepare and speak using the prompt below.

speakingTask.title: Task 7: Expressing Opinions
speakingTask.scenario: Some people believe it is better to have a job you love that pays less, while others prefer a well-paid job they find boring. Which do you think is better? Support your opinion with reasons.
tips: State your opinion clearly.
Give two or three reasons with examples.
Acknowledge the other side briefly.
speakingTask.sampleAnswer: In my opinion, a job you enjoy is better, even if it pays somewhat less. People spend a huge part of their lives at work, so daily satisfaction matters a great deal. When you enjoy what you do, you tend to learn faster, perform better, and often earn promotions over time. I also think stress from a job you dislike can affect your health and relationships. Of course, money is important, and everyone needs to cover basic expenses. But as long as your income is comfortable, I would choose meaningful work every time.

sections.title: Speaking Task 8 · Describing an Unusual Situation
sections.instructions: Prepare and speak using the prompt below.

speakingTask.title: Task 8: Describing an Unusual Situation
speakingTask.scenario: You see a photo of a café where customers sit on swings instead of chairs, and the tables hang from the ceiling on ropes. Describe the café to a friend and explain whether you would recommend visiting it.
tips: Describe the most unusual features first.
Explain how customers might feel or behave there.
Give a clear recommendation with a reason.
speakingTask.sampleAnswer: This café is unlike any place I've seen. Instead of chairs, there are wooden swings, and the tables hang from the ceiling on thick ropes, so everything sways gently. Customers probably feel like kids again, laughing as they try to balance their cups. I would definitely recommend it for a fun outing, though I would not go with a large laptop or a very hot drink. It looks like a place for conversation and photos, not for quiet work.
